# Thyroid surgery

*Categories: Clinical knowledge > Internal medicine > Endocrinology > Thyroid and parathyroid gland disorders > Thyroid surgery*

[Original Article Link](/library/wl0h_T)

---

## Summary

<u>Thyroid</u> <u>surgery</u> is a procedure commonly performed to treat benign and malignant <u>thyroid disorders</u>. <u>Total thyroidectomy</u> entails the removal of the entire <u>thyroid gland</u> and is indicated in the management of <u>thyroid cancer</u> or benign <u>thyroid</u> conditions that affect the entire gland (e.g., <u>Graves disease</u>, multinodular <u>goiter</u>). A small cuff of tissue adjacent to the tracheoesophageal groove is spared in near-total and <u>subtotal thyroidectomy</u> in order to protect the <u>parathyroid glands</u> and the adjacent nerves. <u>Lobectomy</u> (removal of a single lobe) or <u>hemithyroidectomy</u> (removal of a single lobe with the <u>isthmus</u>) is performed for unilateral benign <u>thyroid disorders</u> (e.g., <u>toxic adenoma</u>, recurrent <u>thyroid cysts</u>) and for small, low-risk differentiated <u>thyroid cancers</u>. <u>Postoperative complications</u> include <u>hematoma</u> formation, <u>hypoparathyroidism</u>, nerve palsy (recurrent/<u>superior laryngeal nerve</u>), and <u>hypothyroidism</u>. The greater the extent of resection, the greater the risk of complications. However, the most extensive resections (<u>total thyroidectomy</u>) are associated with the lowest rates of recurrent disease.

## Thyroid gland anatomy

See <u>thyroid gland and parathyroid glands</u>.



* Nerves in close proximity to the <u>thyroid gland</u>  

* <u>Recurrent laryngeal nerve</u> (close to the <u>inferior thyroid artery</u>)

* <u>Superior laryngeal nerve</u> (close to the superior <u>thyroid</u> <u>artery</u>)

## Preparation

* Achieve <u>euthyroid</u> status preoperatively.

* In <u>hyperthyroidism</u> to minimize the risk of <u>thyroid storm</u>

* <u>Thioamides</u>

* Iodides (<u>potassium iodide</u>)

* <u>Beta blockers</u> (e.g., <u>propranolol</u>)

* In <u>hypothyroidism</u>: <u>thyroid hormone</u> replacement

* Preoperative oral <u>calcium</u> and <u>vitamin D</u> supplementation

* Preoperative direct/indirect <u>laryngoscopy</u>

## Technique/steps

| Procedure | Description | Indication |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Total thyroidectomy | <br>* The entire <u>thyroid gland</u> is removed.<br><br> | <br><br>* <u>Thyroid cancer</u><br><br>* Some cases of <u>Graves disease</u> and <u>toxic multinodular goiter</u><br><br>* Large <u>goiter</u> causing obstructive symptoms or physical disfigurement<br><br><br> |
| Near-total thyroidectomy | <br>* A small cuff of <u>thyroid</u> tissue  is left behind<br><br> | <br>* Benign <u>thyroid</u> conditions that affect the entire gland (e.g., large <u>goiter</u>, <u>toxic MNG</u>, <u>Graves disease</u>)<br><br> |
| Subtotal thyroidectomy | <br>* A larger cuff  of <u>thyroid</u> tissue is left behind<br><br> |  |
| Thyroid lobectomy | <br>* Removal of the affected <u>thyroid</u> lobe<br><br> | <br><br>* Low-risk differentiated <u>thyroid cancer</u><br><br>* <u>Follicular adenoma</u><br><br>* <u>Toxic adenoma</u><br><br>* <u>Thyroid cysts</u><br><br><br> |
| Hemithyroidectomy | <br>* The affected lobe with the <u>isthmus</u> is removed.<br><br> |  |

## Complications

* Transient/permanent postoperative hypoparathyroidism (most common)  or <u>hypothyroidism</u>

* <u>Hematoma</u>

* Transient/permanent RLN palsy

* <u>Superior laryngeal nerve</u> palsy → <u>paralysis</u> of <u>cricothyroid muscle</u> → easy voice fatigability; change in the timbre of voice

* <u>Thyroid storm</u>: if the <u>surgery</u> was performed in inadequately treated patients with <u>hyperthyroidism</u> (see "complications" of <u>hyperthyroidism</u> for further details)





|  | Unilateral RLN palsy | Bilateral RLN palsy |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Clinical features | <br><br>* Husky/hoarse voice<br><br>* Ineffective <u>cough</u><br><br>* Risk of <u>aspiration pneumonia</u><br><br><br> | <br>* Immediate postoperative <u>dyspnea</u>, <u>stridor</u> (on <u>extubation</u>)<br><br> |
